AUTHOR: Khiem
TITLE: A novel approach combining YOLO and DeepSORT for detecting and counting live fish in natural environments through video
REGION: not stated (public FishTrac dataset videos; five habitat types)
SPECIES: fish (single presence class, no species labels)
DATA: FishTrac public dataset (Mandel et al. 2023): 9,002 frames extracted from 13 videos across flooded tree roots, shallow coastal, coral reef, bleached coral reef and seagrass habitats
D2: 80/10/10 (train 7,184 / test 909 / validation 909 frames), stratified by habitat (Table 1)
D_EV: Preliminaries: 'This dataset was divided into three parts: a training set (80%), a test set (10%) and a validation set (10%). The division was performed across the corresponding environments'
R_EV: Preliminaries: 'These videos were collected from FishTrac dataset'; Table 1 splits the same 9,002 frames into train/test/validation (single dataset)
E_EV: Discussion: 'The results demonstrate a high accuracy in counting, with a mAP50 of 89.5%.' (only detection mAP reported; counts shown in Fig 12 are not evaluated)
ARCH: YOLOv10 detector + DeepSORT tracker (Kalman filter, Hungarian assignment; max_age 60, n_init 8)
METR: mAP50 (89.5%), mAP50-95, precision, recall, training losses, per-image processing time
NOTE: Frames from 13 FishTrac videos split 8:1:1 at frame level stratified by habitat; whether the split was random is not stated and frames from the same video almost certainly appear in train and test (not discussed).
